title: Zariski cancellation and affine fibrations over the complex numbers
manuscript_title: An explicit failure of complex affine-space cancellation (OpenAI, September 23, 2026)

main_statement.latex: Let $p,s,u,F,J$ be algebraically independent over $\kk$, and set $P=\kk[p,s,u,F,J]$, $x=s^2+u^3+p^2F$, $H=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2-pu$, $A=P/(H)$. \begin{theorem}\label{thm:main} The algebra $A$ in \eqref{eq:example} is an integral complex algebra of dimension four. For an independent variable $w$, \[ A[w]\simeq\kk\poly5, \qquad A\not\simeq\kk\poly4. \] Consequently the Zariski cancellation problem over the complex numbers has a negative answer in dimension four. \end{theorem}
main_statement.paraphrase: An explicit hypersurface X=Spec A in A^5_C, cut out by one polynomial H in p,s,u,F,J, is a 4-dimensional integral affine variety with X x A^1 ≅ A^5 but X not ≅ A^4. So Zariski cancellation fails over C in dimension 4 (first characteristic-zero counterexample in any dimension >= 3).

headline_corollaries.paraphrase: Cor stable-coordinate: H is a coordinate of P[w] but not of P; the Stable Coordinate Conjecture fails over C in ambient dimension 5 after one stabilization.

Cor affine-fibrations: p: X -> A^1 and (p,H): A^5 -> A^2 are smooth surjective A^3-fibrations (every residue-field fiber is A^3) that are not Zariski-locally trivial; Dolgachev-Weisfeiler fails in relative dimension 3 over A^1 and A^2.

abbrev P := MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℂ
def p : P := MvPolynomial.X 0
def s : P := MvPolynomial.X 1
def u : P := MvPolynomial.X 2
def F : P := MvPolynomial.X 3
def J : P := MvPolynomial.X 4

lean_route_differences: Domain and dimension: paper uses UFD irreducibility + transcendence degree; Lean derives both from the explicit cylinder iso (A ↪ A[w] ≅ C^[5]; dim A[w]=dim A+1).

Degeneration: paper uses ord_p from S_{pS} and computes gr A with exact representatives; Lean uses the Rees algebra B=C[q,...]/(H_top - q^3pu) ⊂ A[T^±] and proves B/qB ≅ G directly (Rees.backRed_red).
Positive invariant: Lean produces a possibly non-homogeneous LND on G (Rees scaling + primitive reduction), not the homogeneous D_0 of the paper.

Lifting: paper uses Pic(A^1 x X)=Pic(X) + Brion normalized linearization + uniqueness under sigma_lambda; Lean uses the rational slice theorem (G ↪ F[t], D -> d/dt), a Bezout SL2 frame over the Euclidean ring F[t], and a replica cD to clear denominators, then restores homogeneity by taking the highest valuation component on G~. No Picard groups, no smoothness of G, no faithful flatness.
Final step of rigidity: paper uses R~∩C(a,d,u)=C[a,d,u] and nonnegative weights; Lean writes E'=h·δ and uses sl2 highest-weight theory (SL2.no_negative_highest).
Mason-Stothers: paper re-proves; Lean uses Mathlib Polynomial.abc.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found. I read all seven sections line by line and re-checked every displayed polynomial identity with sympy: xy-z(z+1)=p^2(H+pu); Delta fixes x,y,z with Delta H=p^3, Delta^2H=0; the (L,M) inverse; H(L) expansion; C formula; root divisibility H(L*) in p^3B; H+p^3w=L-ph; the e0 certificate; p^3 | H(L*+p^3Z); xy=z(z+1) in R~; f=C1 v, g=b^2 v, v=alpha f+beta g, alpha C1+beta b^2=1 mod ac-bd-1; E_+ example; fiber weight of v=2; auxiliary degrees (relation 0, N 6, a^3b -3). The logical chain (positive invariant -> lift -> V invariant -> case split -> rigidity) is sound as written. More importantly, the Lean formalization proves the exact headline (all five conjuncts) with no sorry/axiom, by a partly different route; if the comparator check passed, the main theorem is machine-verified.
checked: Lemma induced-lnd: deg is a valuation so each monomial in generators has degree equal to its weight; the shift bound and D_0 != 0 via a maximizing generator are correct.
Prop positive-invariant: F_0A is a subalgebra not containing F (deg 2), so some coordinate has positive degree; d/dq_i kills it.
Prop extracted-lnd Case 2: D~(v)=2 tau V D~(tau) (since D~V=0) and nu(v)=2m give nu(E v)=m-1 and nu(E^2 v) would be -2. Odd j forced since D~(tau) not in tau G~.

Prop rigidity: highest auxiliary component of E^2(v)=0 in degree 6+2lambda is (E')^2(N); coprimality of summands from deg N(q)<=1; abc yields D_u=0, D_d=D_a; leading-coefficient identity gives -u^3 a square in K=C(a,d,b)(u), impossible by u-adic order; ah=E'(b), dh=E'(c); h in C[a,d,u] has weight e-2<0. (Argument works for e<=1, stronger than needed.)
Prop principalization: charts and transition functions; tensoring the injection needs flatness (proved via Laurent charts).
Cor affine-fibrations: residue-field fibers via residual coordinate; Jacobian ideal is unit; local triviality -> locally polynomial -> Sym of projective (BCW) -> free (Suslin over C[p] or C[p,q]).
residual_concerns: Extraordinary claim (first char-0 cancellation counterexample), unreviewed. The Lean proof is the strongest evidence; we did not run Lean/comparator (not installed), so trust rests on the published comparator pass.

Corollaries (SCC failure, Dolgachev-Weisfeiler failure) are NOT formalized and depend on cited theorems (Dutta-Lahiri Thm 3.4, BCW, Suslin) applied to the Lean-verified Thm main; their hypotheses look satisfied but are unchecked by machine.

Paper's Section 4 relies on Picard invariance and normalized linearization re-proved in a few lines (Weil divisor argument). These are correct for smooth affine X but are not needed by Lean, so any slip there would not affect the main theorem's truth.

The paper asserts 'Every additive action on the smooth affine base Spec G lifts uniquely' (01:210-213); uniqueness relies on C[t]^*=C^* for domains C, which holds; smoothness of G is proved but only used for regularity in the Pic step.
